sources.name: Taoyuan A1/A2 accident corridor export, ROC 114
Taoyuan annual A1/A2 accident count by time, ROC 114
Taoyuan A1/A2 party age, vehicle and action status, ROC 114

corridor_export.interpretation: Exact repetition is structural rather than safely removable duplication. The public fields do not expose a unique accident/case identifier, so event grain remains unresolved.

party_export.interpretation: Party-order distributions strongly support a party-related explanation for corridor-row multiplicity, especially in the higher-order tail, but the sources do not reconcile exactly. The party product excludes some classes of parties/cases and cannot be joined to corridor coordinates with the published fields.

road_sidewalk_join.interpretation: A substantial partial road-name join is feasible, but permissive normalization gains roughly 11-16 percentage points of coverage and may introduce false matches. It is a sensitivity path, not a verified production join.

sidewalk_quality.interpretation: The table mixes aggregate and road-level rows and contains values requiring plausibility review. Cleaning must distinguish summary rows from suspected field errors rather than applying blind clipping.

coordinate_recurrence.interpretation: These are recurrence candidates only. They are not risk rates or claims that a location is dangerous because exposure and true event grain are unresolved.

facts_upgraded: Official row-level accident and sidewalk resources are retrievable and reproducibly analyzable.
Accident coordinates are present and valid under a broad Taoyuan bounding-box check.
Road-name enrichment has measurable but incomplete coverage.
The party dataset confirms pedestrian/person participation exists in the wider official data ecosystem.
new_uncertainties: The analytical grain of the corridor export is not explicit; exact repetition is structural and cannot simply be deduplicated.
Party characteristics and corridor coordinates are published in separate products without a common public case identifier.
Sidewalk rows contain embedded aggregate records, zero-heavy road-length fields, duplicate district-road keys and suspect width values.
No pedestrian or traffic exposure denominator has been established.
claims_blocked: The 94,183 corridor rows cannot be described as 94,183 independent crashes from these files alone.
Exact full-row deduplication cannot be described as correct event-level cleaning.
Road-name co-location with sidewalk width cannot establish pedestrian risk or causality.
No corridor should be publicly labeled dangerous or recommended for intervention from this probe.
problem_packet_effects.recommended_reframe: Determine whether Taoyuan's published accident, party and infrastructure data can be reconciled into a defensible pedestrian-corridor investigation before any risk ranking or intervention proposal.
